speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any triggers like exercise, cold air, or specific environments? Also, do these symptoms wake you up at night or occur only during the day?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since your symptoms worsen with exertion and at night, are you currently taking any medications like beta-blockers or aspirin, and have you noticed any wheezing or a "tightness" in your chest? Also, given the illness you had 8 weeks ago, have you had any follow-up tests since then?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-viral Cough Variant Asthma.

The history of a recent upper respiratory infection followed by exertion-induced and nocturnal cough is highly suggestive of reactive airway disease triggered by the preceding viral illness. Given the lack of fever at this stage and the specific triggers, this fits the profile better than a persistent infection or heart failure. No further tests are required at this moment; we will initiate a trial of inhaled corticosteroids and a bronchodilator to confirm the diagnosis clinically.
